source_row.stem: A client with lung cancer develops facial/neck swelling, distended neck veins, and dyspnea, worse when lying flat. The nurse should suspect:
source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A simple allergic reaction, since facial swelling and dyspnea are thought to typically reflect a hypersensitivity response","B":"A normal finding that would not usually prompt further evaluation in a client with lung cancer","C":"Heart failure exclusively, since positional dyspnea and neck vein distention are thought to typically point to this cause","D":"Superior vena cava syndrome, an oncologic emergency from tumor compression of the SVC"}}
source_row.rationale: Facial/neck swelling, distended neck veins, and dyspnea worse when supine are classic signs of superior vena cava syndrome, an oncologic emergency from tumor compression obstructing venous return.
